title: Man-at-Arms
name: Barristan
description: The Man-at-Arms is an old soldier who lost his rank in disgrace and has fought as a common one ever since. He wants no command, but in battle his voice still carries like an officer's, bellowing encouragement to his allies and threats at the enemy. Beneath the gruffness he is one of the kindest men on any field, and the first to shoulder another's burden.
history: The Man-at-Arms was an ambitious young officer who climbed by politics rather than battle, and won a command before he had ever seen a fight. He led his regiment to its death. In the field hospital, their ghosts came for him every night, until he clawed out an eye to be rid of them. Stripped of his rank, he went back to war as a common soldier, and has fought in other men's trenches ever since, expecting to die in one.
summary: A gruff, kind-hearted old soldier, once a disgraced officer, seeking atonement on one battlefield after another.

appearance.features: Grey beard and moustache, a scar across the brow

clothing.head: None
clothing.body: Steel breastplate and pauldrons over a red-and-gold tunic
clothing.accessories: Eyepatch over the right eye, a medal pinned at the chest

notes: Still speaks in a tactician's vocabulary from his training (stratagems, manoeuvres), mixed with barracks familiarity (lad, greenhorn)
Still has the quick tongue of a man who once rose by wit, though these days he mostly turns it on his own age and waistline
Tells war stories freely, but privately broods over every decision he made in them
Swears in old soldier's curses (sod off, bollocking) and drops his h's
Disapproves of other people's dice, pipeweed and drink, and advises against them, but never orders anyone to stop
